papers.title: Replacing Large Language Models with Jev Decision Models for Low-Latency Edge Service Orchestration
papers.summary: Jev, a small decision model, cuts median decision time by 22.7-64.5% against the fastest large model. On a live path, Jev keeps 0.91-0.95 of requests exact and on time; large models fall below 0.1.
papers.practicalUseCase: Route edge requests with a small decision model when each request has few fixed fields.
papers.limitation: Wide requests with many fields are the limit. Jev also loses a few exact-match points on four-field requests.

papers.title: Persona Dosing: Calibrated Activation Steering for Graded Trait Control
papers.summary: PersonaDose sets how strongly a model shows a trait. It beats a standard method by 33.2, 18.3 and 17.8 points on three models.
papers.practicalUseCase: Set a persona strength for a chatbot with one calibrated number instead of guessing a steering value.
papers.limitation: Only 14-22 of 28 target strengths are reachable per model. Text stays coherent on held-out questions for some traits only.

papers.title: Ego2Act: Evaluating Goal-Directed Manipulation in Egocentric Video Generation
papers.summary: Video models often skip or half-do steps in 110 daily tasks (2,640 videos). Later steps then lack the needed state, so the goal fails.
papers.practicalUseCase: Do not trust a video model as a robot planner for multi-step tasks without checking each step.
papers.limitation: The benchmark covers hand manipulation in first-person video only. The abstract gives no per-model scores.

papers.title: MemFold: Learning Compact Soft Memory for Long-Context Personalization via On-Policy Optimization
papers.summary: MemFold packs a user's long history into a fixed number of vectors. It scores highest on PersonaMem-32K and PersonaMem-128K, and the lead grows with longer history.
papers.practicalUseCase: Give a long-running assistant a fixed-size memory so its input does not grow with each chat.
papers.limitation: Tests use three Qwen model families and a few memory benchmarks. The abstract gives no exact accuracy numbers.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.summary: Sustainability committees raise bank environmental scores. In Islamic banks, only overall and resource scores rise, which the authors call symbolic; conventional banks improve in all four areas.
papers.practicalUseCase: Islamic banks that set up a sustainability committee should also track green product launches, not only the overall score.
papers.limitation: Panel regressions show links, not cause. The study covers emerging markets only.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.summary: Across 11,944 sukuk issues (2012-2022), sustainability sukuk stay tiny and sit mostly in Indonesia, Malaysia and Saudi Arabia. Equity-based contracts bring larger issues than sale-based ones.
papers.practicalUseCase: An issuer who wants a bigger sustainability sukuk should consider an equity-based contract and a USD or Euro denomination.
papers.limitation: The data ends in 2022. It shows links between traits and issue size, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.summary: In 15 Jordanian Islamic banks (214 managers), AI, big data and data management raise competitiveness and sustainable development. Staff digital skill raises only competitiveness.
papers.practicalUseCase: A bank should fund AI tools and data management first. Staff digital training alone will not lift sustainability results.
papers.limitation: The survey is cross-sectional and covers Jordan only. It shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.summary: ICT adoption is the strongest driver of growth in 218 banks across 12 countries. High-tech exports help only when combined with ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Put digital infrastructure first when planning bank expansion. Strong governance supports the gain, mainly for Islamic banks.
papers.limitation: Only 12 countries are covered. Panel data shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.summary: In OIC countries, income, tertiary education, institutional quality and internet access drive financial inclusion. The data covers 35 OIC and OECD countries from 2005 to 2021.
papers.practicalUseCase: Policy makers in OIC countries should fund internet access, education and women and youth programs to widen inclusion.
papers.limitation: The study covers 35 countries and one estimator. It shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.summary: Impostor feelings are frequent in medical students. Rates vary a lot by sampling method and region.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you feel like a fraud in a tough program, know that it is common. Share it with peers or mentors.
papers.limitation: The abstract gives no pooled rate. Differences between studies are large, so the pooled figure is shaky.

papers.title: Psychometric properties of the Arabic Perceived Digital Well-Being Scale (PDWS) in Saudi young adults
papers.institution: Imam Mohammad ibn Saud Islamic University
papers.summary: The Arabic digital well-being scale shows three domains: emotional, social and cognitive. Scores rise with life satisfaction and fall with fear of missing out.
papers.practicalUseCase: Use this scale to check whether your phone use helps or hurts your mood, social life and focus.
papers.limitation: The sample came from social media in Riyadh. The design shows links, not cause.
